form.title: Contact form
form.empty: The form opens when you answer a call. To transfer you need a location, an incident type and at least one agency.
form.loc_none: No location: type the street or click the map.
form.loc_unknown_street: Street not found in the directory.
form.confirm_incomplete: Incomplete form ({list}): the dispatcher will have to ask again. Press again to transfer anyway.

db.note_abandoned_ring: The caller hung up before an answer: a ringing line should be picked up within seconds.
db.note_abandoned_hold: The caller hung up on hold: agitated callers can't wait long.
db.note_abandoned_queue: The caller hung up while queued at the switchboard.
db.note_wrong_address: The agitated caller gave a wrong address: asking again after calming them would have revealed the error.
db.note_far: The location you set is {m} m from the real one.
db.note_transferred_improper: Not an emergency: transferring it tied up resources needed elsewhere.
db.note_competence: Jurisdiction: {required} was needed, {sent} was dispatched. Handing over between forces costs minutes.
db.note_duplicate_transfer: Incident already transferred: this call should have been merged, not transferred again.
db.note_incomplete: Incomplete form: the dispatcher had to ask the questions again.
db.note_closed_emergency: This was a real emergency, but the call was closed without a transfer.
db.note_wrong_merge: Merged into a different incident: this emergency got no help.
db.note_dropped_emergency: The caller hung up before the emergency was transferred.
db.note_classification: The incident type doesn't match what really happened.
db.note_missing_facts: Some critical information was not collected.
db.note_panic: The caller stayed panicked: a reassuring line would have made answers more reliable.
db.note_called_back: The caller called back at {time}: the incident outcome depends on how the callback was handled.

tutor.welcome: Welcome to the Valdemara 112 control room. As a call-taker you answer, work out what's happening, locate the incident and transfer the call to the right agency. The clock at the top runs in real time during calls and speeds up when the room is quiet.
tutor.lines: On the left are the 4 lines. When one rings, the bar under the number is the caller's patience: when it runs out, they hang up. Below is the log of everything that happens.
tutor.ring: A line is ringing. Answer with the «Answer» button or the line's number key.
tutor.dialog: In the middle is the conversation. Every question takes a few seconds while other lines wait: choose carefully. Watch the caller's state at the top: panicked callers may give wrong answers.
tutor.ask_address: Location first. Pick the address question and wait for the answer.
tutor.facts: Here is what the caller told you, in their own words. It's not a diagnosis: interpreting it is your job.
tutor.place: Enter the location in the contact form: type the street, with suggestions from the directory, and the house number. Or click the right spot on the map.
tutor.map: The white mark on the map is the location you set. For mobiles a dashed circle shows the phone's estimated position, invaluable when the caller doesn't know where they are. The form also shows the territorial jurisdiction, State Police or Carabinieri.
tutor.ask_access: The woman is on the floor and can't get up. Who will open the door for the responders? Ask her.
tutor.event: Choose the incident category and type: it's a fall at home, so «Medical» and «Fall injury».
tutor.agencies: She's alone and the door is locked: you need 118, and the fire brigade to get in. Select both.
tutor.transfer: Now transfer. If minimum data is missing (location, type, agency) the form warns you first.
tutor.prank: Another call is coming in. Answer it.
tutor.prank_listen: Something's off. Ask a couple of questions and listen carefully: what's in the background?
tutor.prank_close: It's a prank. Under «Duplicate or not an emergency» choose «Prank call» and close it. Free the line quickly, but only after checking.
tutor.fire: A fire report: handle it on your own. Location, type, agency, transfer. And always ask whether anyone is hurt.
tutor.witness: Another passer-by is calling about the same bin. Don't transfer it again: under «Duplicate or not an emergency» merge it into the incident already transferred.
tutor.hold: If another line rings while you're talking, press H to put the current call on hold and resume it later, but agitated callers don't wait long. P pauses the shift.
tutor.done: Training complete. At the end of each shift you get a grade and a call-by-call debrief showing what really happened. In real shifts calls come whenever they like, even three at once. Good luck.
